transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... I guess I'm just having a hard time slowing down. It feels like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. I'll finish one thing at school, or at home, and... I just immediately jump into the next thing. I just can't really seem to shut myself off.
Has this feeling of being 'on a motor' and unable to slow down been present since you were a child, or is this a new change for you recently?

No, it's... not new. It's been this way for a long time. My mother used to joke that back in elementary school, I was the one teaching the class... mostly because I was always out of my seat, or talking. I guess I had a habit of cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, it's just... been part of who I am since I was a kid. It didn't just start with this... family change recently.
Do you also find it hard to stay focused on tasks—like losing track of details, making careless mistakes, or forgetting things you need to do—separate from feeling restless or impulsive?
Um... no. Not really. I keep track of things fine, mostly. It's just... the other stuff. I don't really make a lot of mistakes like that.
Do you notice this restlessness and impulsivity happening in more than one setting—like at home, at school or work, and when you're with friends—or is it mainly limited to just one place?

Yeah... it's everywhere. It's not just one place. 

Um... at work, things got... well, there were complaints. It got serious enough that they put me on a corrective plan. And at home... my spouse says I just make the caregiving routines harder. Like they have to manage my energy on top of everything else. 

I don't know. I'm trying to help, but... I feel like I'm just damaging trust with everyone. My colleagues, my family... it's just everywhere.
Beyond the restlessness and impulsivity, have you noticed a pattern of getting into fights, breaking rules, lying, stealing, or being deliberately defiant toward authority figures?
No. I don't... I don't do things like that. I'm a teacher, I... I follow the rules. I don't get into fights or steal. It's just the... the energy, like I said. Not... not anything malicious.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong (childhood-onset) pattern of hyperactivity and impulsivity—motor restlessness, inability to stay still, interrupting/blurting out, and impulsive behavior—that has persisted into adulthood. Symptoms are pervasive across multiple settings (work and home) and cause clear functional impairment (corrective work plan, marital/family strain). Inattentive symptoms (careless mistakes, forgetfulness, disorganization) are explicitly denied, ruling out the combined or inattentive presentations. Conduct-disordered or oppositional behaviors (fighting, stealing, lying, defiance) are also denied, arguing against a disruptive behavior disorder. This clinical picture is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation (F90.1).
